bull_bear.body:
- Long-term, strategic holding company with significant, stable stakes in established Bajaj Group financial services and automotive entities.
- Low standalone business risk due to passive investment management and long-term holding horizon.
- Lean operational structure with only 14 employees, supported by group companies under an MoU, enabling high quality at low cost.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration risk to Bajaj group companies — BHIL's standalone risk is low, but risks arising from businesses of group companies are its key risks. Its value is heavily tied to the performance and risk profiles of Bajaj Auto and Bajaj Finserv.
- Market risk on investment portfolio — As an investment company holding listed and unlisted securities, BHIL is exposed to market risk from fluctuations in the value of its equity holdings.
- Governance and reputation risk — BHIL explicitly flags governance risk and reputation risk as key exposures, given its role as a group holding company and the interconnectedness with promoter-group entities.
- Regulatory risk from RBI reclassification — The Company has applied for voluntary surrender of its NBFC-ICC registration to become an Unregistered CIC. Failure to obtain RBI approval could impact its operating structure and compliance requirements.
- Credit risk — Credit risk is identified as a key risk exposure, likely relating to its treasury operations and investments in debt securities.
- Compliance risk — Compliance risk is flagged as a key risk, given the multi-layered regulatory framework applicable to an NBFC investment company and its listed status.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: BHIL is registered as an NBFC-ICC and operates as a holding and investment company with no other operations of its own. It earns revenue primarily through dividends from investments held in group companies, with strategic stakes in Bajaj Finserv Ltd., Bajaj Auto Ltd., and their subsidiaries. The Company is pursuing voluntary surrender of its NBFC registration to reclassify as an Unregistered Core Investment Company.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Pursue the main strategic objective of a group investment holding company, holding long-term equity stakes in Bajaj group operating companies.
- Consolidate ownership of key group financial services entities, as demonstrated by the acquisition of Allianz SE's stake in Bajaj General Insurance and Bajaj Life Insurance to achieve 100% group holding.
- The Company has not paid any commission or sitting fees to independent directors for attending separate meetings of independent directors historically; the Board approved payment of sitting fees and commission for such meetings effective 30 May 2025. No public, rights, bonus, or preferential issue of shares was made during the year. The Company does not accept deposits.
- CSR obligation for FY2026 was H 42.57 crore, with H 27.07 crore spent and H 15.55 crore transferred to unspent CSR account for ongoing multi-year projects with milestone-based payments.
- Board-approved Responsible and Sustainable Business Conduct Policy covers all NGRBC principles; SGS India provided Reasonable Assurance for Core and Limited Assurance for BRSR Comprehensive.
- Zero tolerance towards unethical business practices and bribery in any form, enforced through a Code of Ethics and Personal Conduct (CoEPC).
- 100% of Board, KMPs, and employees covered by training and awareness programmes on code of conduct, insider trading, ESG, prevention of sexual harassment, and anti-money laundering.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY2026, the Company acquired a 17.56% equity stake in each of Bajaj General Insurance Ltd. and Bajaj Life Insurance Ltd. from Allianz SE, which, together with acquisitions by associate Bajaj Finserv Ltd. and promoter group company Jamnalal Sons Pvt. Ltd., resulted in the group collectively holding 100% of the equity share capital of both insurance subsidiaries. This marks a key milestone in Bajaj Group's financial services expansion.

- Risks arising out of businesses of the group companies are the key risks of the Company.

sk.overview: India's digital financial services and NBFC-led retail lending sector serves a large, young, credit-underpenetrated mass market. Formalization (GST, JAM/India Stack, eKYC), rising smartphone/internet penetration and low data costs are enabling tech-led NBFCs and fintechs to underwrite and serve borrowers that conventional banks have historically underserved, particularly in unsecured personal loans and loan-against-property.
sk.schemes: Digital India|JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) / India Stack|eKYC / DigiLocker|OCEN / ONDC|PMJDY financial inclusion|Udyam / MSME formalization
sk.structure: NBFCs hold ~18-19% of systemic credit and ~23% of the combined personal-loans and LAP market (FY2025), accounting for 25% of personal loans and 21% of LAP. Tech-led NBFCs/fintechs (Kissht, Moneyview, KreditBee, Fibe) capture share from cautious conventional lenders via digital-first, AI/ML …
